# specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md

> For agentic workers: REQUIRED SKILL: derive-roadmap — resume via its
> reconcile step; route each unticked stage per its ROUTING line; never plan
> this document wholesale.

## Outcomes

Source: partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md`, `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md` (both PROPOSED; the spec's §2.2 puts O2 and O3 out of its own scope).
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). A uv workspace with the four scaffold packages `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download`, `sec-edgar-index-ingest` and `sec-edgar-ingest`.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small. About 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, which is minutes of downloading at 3 req/s (basis: SEC full-index and daily-index directories). Measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large. Millions of files and weeks for full history at 3 req/s (basis: index row count × request rate; not yet measured). Per-quarter cost measured by Stage 2 |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk (basis: none yet). Measured by Stage 3 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

The order follows the partner's ranking (O1 → O2 → O3), and dependency gives the same order: each outcome reads the previous one's output. The hardening stages (4–7) come after the three outcome stages. The full-history submissions download (Stage 6) waits for Stage 2's measured per-quarter cost.

- [ ] Stage 1: Index table, core
      Objective: Ingest every real quarterly master index since 1993, plus the open quarter's daily master indexes, into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (scaffolds only)
      Produces: one queryable filing-index table on local disk, with daily/quarterly overlap deduplicated; `specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md`
      Exit: O1 — the table holds rows from every quarterly file through the last closed quarter and every open-quarter daily file, with no duplicate filing keys. The findings file records the files fetched, total bytes, row count and wall-clock time of the real run.
      Leaves out: index manifest and versioned publication (Stage 4); replay from raw snapshots (Stage 4); legacy-format golden fixtures (Stage 4); index reconciliation and withdrawals (Stage 5); shared request budget (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions, one quarter
      Objective: Download the submissions that one real quarter's index rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: one quarter's submissions on disk, each traceable to its index row; the measured per-quarter download cost
      Exit: O2 — every submission named by the chosen quarter's index rows is on disk or listed as a gap with its reason. The measured files, bytes and elapsed time for that quarter are recorded.
      Leaves out: full-history submissions backfill (Stage 6); resumable checkpoints (Stage 6); shared request budget (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling, one quarter
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of Stage 2's submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk
      Produces: extracted main documents for that quarter's 10-K and 8-K filings, each linked to its submission
      Exit: O3 — for the Stage 2 quarter, every 10-K and 8-K in the index has an extracted main document or a recorded failure reason. Extraction time and output volume are recorded.
      Leaves out: full-history submissions backfill (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Index manifest, versioned publication and replay
      Objective: Make the index table reproducible from retained raw snapshots, and publish it through versioned generations instead of loose files.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1's ingestion of the index table
      Produces: index manifest and versioned publication; replay from raw snapshots; legacy-format golden fixtures
      Exit: O1 — rebuilding the table from retained raw files with SEC access disabled yields the same logical rows. Readers resolve the current table through one active pointer. Fixtures cover each index format in the ingested range.
      Leaves out: index reconciliation and withdrawals (Stage 5)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Index reconciliation and withdrawals
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes periodically and account for additions, changed fields and withdrawals without discarding history.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 4's index manifest and versioned publication
      Produces: index reconciliation and withdrawals
      Exit: O1 — a re-read of a changed quarter publishes additions and field updates as a new generation. A removal waits for explicit approval. An unchanged quarter is a no-op.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full-history submissions backfill
      Objective: Download every submission the index names, and run 10-K/8-K extraction over all of them, as a resumable campaign.
      Outcomes: O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's per-quarter cost and download path; Stage 3's extraction
      Produces: full-history submissions backfill; resumable checkpoints; shared request budget
      Exit: O2 — every submission named by the index is on disk or listed as a gap, and an interrupted run resumes without refetching completed files. O3 — every 10-K and 8-K in the index has an extracted main document or a recorded failure. All SEC requests stay within one shared rate budget.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling, deployment and monitoring
      Objective: Run daily index ingestion, submission catch-up and reconciliation on a schedule, in a deployed environment, with alerts.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 4–6
      Produces: scheduling and deployment; monitoring and alerts
      Exit: O1 — observed scheduled daily runs ingest new indexes and catch up after a missed run. O2/O3 — the same runs fetch and extract the new filings. Failures and gaps raise alerts.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, and writing-plans copies it verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O3 against the accumulated system, with evidence per verdict (implementing stage/plan, Deviation notes, `specs/deferred_items.md` entries). Each unmet outcome exits as a new stage, or as a conscious deferral with a written reason.

---

Approve this seven-stage partition (three outcome stages, then four hardening stages) and I'll commit it and hand Stage 1 to brainstorming in a fresh session.
